country.name: Bulgaria
country.tagline: Dionysus's homeland, the Cabernet that taught Britain to drink red, and native grapes such as Mavrud and Broadleaf Melnik finding their voice again.

stats.note: Vineyard area: OIV 2025 (58 kha). Production: 66 million litres in 2025 according to the Executive Agency for Vine and Wine (BTA, 2026), 10 to 15% below 2024; OIV reported 712,000 hl for 2024.

country.overview:
Bulgaria sits on one of the oldest wine soils in Europe. The Thracians, who held these lands from the second millennium BC to late antiquity, worshipped a wine god the Greeks later knew as Dionysus, poured libations from gold rhyta and built rock sanctuaries such as Perperikon and the mound temples of Starosel. Archaeologists trace grape growing in the Thracian valley back several thousand years. Two mountain ranges organise the country: the Balkan range (Stara Planina) runs east to west through the middle and splits a continental north from a warmer south, and the Rhodope and Pirin massifs close off the south and south-west.

The modern map has five traditional regions: the Danubian Plain in the north, the Black Sea coast in the east, the Sub-Balkan valley of the Rose Valley beneath the Balkan range, the Thracian Lowlands in the south and the Struma valley in the south-west. Two large PGIs, Thracian Lowlands and Danube Plain, are what most labels actually use. There are also 52 PDOs, a legacy of the socialist-era control system, most named after a town and its old state winery. Critics note that so many PDOs mean little to drinkers, and few producers use them.

The OIV counted about 58,000 ha of vineyard in 2025, down from 145,000 ha at the end of the Second World War. In 2025 the 365 operating wineries (151 with foreign investors) made about 66 million litres, a short crop, while Bulgarians drink 110 to 120 million litres a year. International grapes dominate, roughly 70 percent of the vineyard, but the native varieties carry the interest. Mavrud from Asenovgrad and Perushtitsa makes deep, tannic, blackberry-and-spice reds. Shiroka Melnishka Loza (Broadleaf Melnik) is the late-ripening red of the Struma valley around Melnik, and its offspring Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55) ripens earlier. Rubin, a 1944 Nebbiolo x Syrah cross from Pleven, makes dark, fragrant reds. Gamza (Kadarka) is the light, peppery red of the north-west. Pamid is the old everyday red. Dimyat, a Gouais Blanc offspring, is the Black Sea white, and Misket Cherven (Red Misket) is grown around Sungurlare and Karlovo.

The modern story turns on one export miracle. In the 1970s and 1980s the state export monopoly Vinimpex sold soft, cheap Bulgarian Cabernet Sauvignon to British supermarkets and off-licences. Exports to the UK passed 2 million cases in 1990 and reached 3.3 million by 1994. The collapse after 1989 (slow land restitution, privatisation fights, neglected vineyards) erased that position by the late 1990s. Since EU entry in 2007 a new generation of estates has rebuilt quality, among them Bessa Valley, Castra Rubra, Katarzyna, Terra Tangra, Zagreus, Rumelia, Villa Melnik, Logodaj, Bononia, Burgozone, Tipchenitza and Midalidare.

history.title: Starosel's Thracian temples
history.text: The mound temple of Chetinyova Mogila near Starosel, dated to the late 5th and early 4th centuries BC and excavated from 2000, is the largest of several Thracian cult complexes in the area, now the backdrop to a winery.

history.title: Perperikon, sanctuary of Dionysus
history.text: On a 470 m rock hill near Kardzhali, Perperikon was a sacred site from prehistory to the Middle Ages; a famous temple of Dionysus is thought to have stood here. Excavations by Nikolay Ovcharov began in 2000.

history.title: The Panagyurishte gold
history.text: The Panagyurishte treasure, found in 1949, includes gold rhyta and a phiale used for wine at Thracian feasts, among the finest drinking vessels to survive from antiquity.

history.title: Khan Krum's decree
history.text: Legend says the Bulgarian ruler Khan Krum ordered the vineyards uprooted to curb drunkenness, and that a young man named Mavrud, emboldened by wine, killed a lion, which persuaded Krum to relent and gave the Mavrud grape its name. Like Burebista's Dacian edict, it is more legend than record.

history.title: Kordopulov House, Melnik
history.text: A merchant's house with a rock-cut cellar able to hold about 300 tonnes of wine was built in Melnik in 1754 and later bought by the Greek wine trader Manolis Kordopoulos, who shipped Melnik wine across Europe.

history.title: Liberation and phylloxera
history.text: After liberation from the Ottomans the vineyard grew to about 100,000 ha before phylloxera arrived; by the 1920s only about 45,000 ha remained.

history.title: Breeding new grapes
history.text: Rubin (Nebbiolo x Syrah) was created at the Pleven institute in 1944; Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55) was bred at Sandanski in 1963 from Shiroka Melnishka Loza, with Valdiguié later identified by DNA as the pollen parent.

history.title: Five regions decreed
history.text: A government decree of 13 July 1960 divided Bulgaria into five viticultural regions, the framework still used informally today.

history.title: The British Cabernet boom
history.text: Bulgarian Cabernet Sauvignon became a staple of UK supermarkets; exports to Britain topped 2 million cases in 1990 and reached 3.3 million in 1994 before collapsing as privatisation and land restitution stalled.

history.title: EU entry
history.text: Bulgaria joined the EU and its 52 PDOs and two PGIs were registered; foreign investment followed, and by 2026 151 of 365 wineries had foreign investors.

country.classification: Under EU rules Bulgaria has 52 PDOs (*защитено наименование за произход*, ZNP) and two PGIs (*защитено географско указание*): Тракийска низина (Thracian Lowlands) and Дунавска равнина (Danube Plain). The PDOs, registered in 2007 (Bolyarovo in 2009), are mostly named after a town and its surrounding municipalities, inherited from the socialist-era Controliran (DGO/DGOC) system; most serious producers prefer the two PGIs, which are flexible and widely recognised. The Executive Agency for Vine and Wine (IAVV) supervises the system. Traditional terms include *резерва* (reserve), *специална резерва* and *премиум*.
country.climate_soils: North of the Balkan range the Danubian Plain is temperate continental with hot summers and cold winters, on chernozem and loess. The Black Sea coast is milder and humid, good for whites. The Thracian Lowlands south of the Balkan range are warmer and drier, with Mediterranean influence moving up the Maritsa valley. Soils there are cinnamon forest soils, smolnitsa (black clay) and alluvium. The Struma valley in the south-west is the warmest corner, almost Mediterranean, with sandstone and sandy soils around Melnik.

grapes.name: Mavrud
grapes.note: Late, low-yielding native red of Asenovgrad and Perushtitsa (about 2% of plantings): dark, tannic, blackberry and spice.

grapes.name: Shiroka Melnishka Loza
grapes.note: Broadleaf Melnik, endemic to the Struma valley around Melnik; late-ripening, spicy, oak-friendly; reportedly Winston Churchill's favourite Bulgarian wine.

grapes.name: Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55)
grapes.note: Early Melnik, bred at Sandanski in 1963 from Broadleaf Melnik and Valdiguié; riper, rounder and easier.

grapes.name: Rubin
grapes.note: Nebbiolo x Syrah cross from Pleven (1944): deep colour, violet perfume, firm structure.

grapes.name: Gamza
grapes.note: Kadarka, the light, peppery red of the north-west Danube plain (Vidin, Suhindol, Pavlikeni).

grapes.name: Pamid
grapes.note: Old, light, low-acid native red, once the most planted grape in the country.

grapes.name: Dimyat
grapes.note: Black Sea white, offspring of Gouais Blanc; fresh, floral, also used for brandy.

grapes.name: Misket Cherven
grapes.note: Red Misket, a pink-skinned aromatic white of Sungurlare and the Rose Valley.

grapes.name: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot
grapes.note: The backbone of the 1980s export boom and still the most planted reds.

regions.name: Danubian Plain
regions.tagline: North Bulgaria between the Danube and the Balkan range: Gamza, Cabernet and the old export wineries.
regions.summary: The Danubian Plain (North Bulgaria) stretches from Vidin in the north-west to Ruse in the east, between the Danube and the Balkan range. It is temperate continental, with hot summers and cold winters, and it produced much of the Cabernet Sauvignon that flooded British shelves in the 1980s from wineries at Suhindol, Svishtov, Pavlikeni and Lyaskovets. Gamza (Kadarka) is the local red, especially around Vidin and Novo Selo, and Pleven's institute bred Rubin. Modern estates include Bononia, Magura, Borovitza, Chateau de Val, Burgozone and Tipchenitza. The PGI Danube Plain (Дунавска равнина) covers the region.
regions.history: Suhindol's cooperative, founded in 1909, is often called the first wine cooperative in Bulgaria; the state wineries of the region supplied the Vinimpex export machine.
regions.terroir: Chernozem and loess plains, limestone and sandstone in the north-west near Belogradchik; Danube influence moderates temperature.
regions.grapes: Gamza, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Rubin, Muscat Ottonel, Chardonnay, Aligoté.
regions.styles: Medium-bodied reds, fresh whites, traditional-method sparkling at Magura.
regions.classification: 13 PDOs plus the Danube Plain PGI.

regions.name: Black Sea
regions.tagline: The north-east and the coast: Dimyat, Riesling and crisp whites near Varna and Pomorie.
regions.summary: The Black Sea region (East Bulgaria) covers the coast from Dobrich to Burgas and the plateau inland around Shumen, Veliki Preslav and Targovishte. The sea moderates the climate and the long autumns suit white grapes: Dimyat, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel, Traminer, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay. The Khan Krum and Preslav cellars are historic white-wine houses; Pomorie, on the southern coast, is known for Dimyat and for brandy.
regions.history: The plateau around Pliska and Preslav was the heart of the First Bulgarian Empire, and Veliki Preslav was its 10th-century capital. Euxinograd, the former royal summer palace near Varna, has kept vineyards on its estate.
regions.terroir: Loess and chernozem on the Dobrudzha plateau, limestone near Shumen, sands near the coast.
regions.grapes: Dimyat, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel, Traminer, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Ugni Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot.
regions.styles: Fresh and aromatic whites, some reds, brandy.
regions.classification: 12 PDOs including the broad Chernomorski Rayon and Yuzhno Chernomorie.

regions.name: Rose Valley
regions.tagline: The Sub-Balkan valley of roses beneath the Balkan range: Red Misket and cool whites.
regions.summary: The Sub-Balkan region (Подбалкански район) is the long valley between the Balkan range and the Sredna Gora, famous for the Kazanlak rose-oil fields. Its vineyards around Karlovo, Sliven, Sungurlare, Karnobat and Shivachevo make Red Misket (Misket Cherven), Muscat and Riesling whites and some reds. Sungurlare's valley is the classic home of Red Misket.
regions.history: The Valley of the Thracian Kings around Kazanlak holds dozens of Thracian tombs, including the UNESCO-listed Kazanlak tomb (4th century BC).
regions.terroir: Alluvial and cinnamon forest soils in a sheltered valley; cooler than Thrace.
regions.grapes: Misket Cherven, Muscat Ottonel, Riesling, Rkatsiteli, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot.

regions.name: Thracian Lowlands
regions.tagline: The Maritsa basin and Sakar hills: Mavrud, Rubin and Bulgaria's richest reds.
regions.summary: The Thracian Lowlands (South Bulgaria) follow the Maritsa river from Pazardzhik through Plovdiv, Stara Zagora and Haskovo to the Turkish and Greek borders, closed off by the Rhodopes to the south. It is the warmest large region and the heart of Bulgarian red wine. Mavrud comes from Asenovgrad and Perushtitsa; Rubin, Cabernet, Merlot and Syrah thrive. The Sakar hills near the Turkish border (Lyubimets, Svilengrad, Harmanli) have become a magnet for modern estates such as Katarzyna, Terra Tangra and Castra Rubra. Bessa Valley near Pazardzhik, Zagreus at Vinitsa, Rumelia and Midalidare are other names to know. The PGI Thracian Lowlands (Тракийска низина) covers the region.
regions.history: Thracian sanctuaries, Philippopolis (Plovdiv) and the Roman road across Thrace made this a wine route since antiquity; Mavrud's legend is set here.
regions.terroir: Cinnamon forest soils, smolnitsa black clays and alluvium; hot, dry summers with Mediterranean influence up the Maritsa valley.
regions.grapes: Mavrud, Rubin, Pamid, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay, Viognier.
regions.classification: 16 PDOs plus the Thracian Lowlands PGI.

regions.name: Struma Valley
regions.tagline: The warm south-west by Greece: Broadleaf Melnik, sandstone pyramids and Bulgaria's smallest town.
regions.summary: The Struma valley (South-West Bulgaria) follows the Struma river south from Blagoevgrad to the Greek border, between the Pirin and Belasitsa mountains. Mediterranean air funnels up the valley, making it Bulgaria's warmest wine area. Its heart is Melnik, a town of about 400 people amid sandstone and conglomerate 'earth pyramids', and its grape is Shiroka Melnishka Loza with its early-ripening offspring Melnik 55. Estates include Villa Melnik, Logodaj, Orbelus, Zlaten Rozhen, Damianitza and Sintica.
regions.history: Melnik's wine was traded to Venice, Austria and England from the 17th and 18th centuries; the town once held about 20,000 people, but most of its Greek population left after 1913. The Kordopulov House cellar of 1754 is its great monument.
regions.terroir: Sandy and sandstone soils, conglomerates and alluvium; hot, dry, sub-Mediterranean.
regions.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55), Keratsuda, Sandanski Misket, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah.
regions.styles: Spicy, oak-aged reds; rare whites from Keratsuda and Sandanski Misket.

bg-asenovgrad.name: Asenovgrad
bg-asenovgrad.summary: Asenovgrad, at the edge of the Rhodopes south-east of Plovdiv, is the traditional heartland of Mavrud, the late-ripening, thick-skinned native red that makes dark, tannic wines with blackberry, mulberry and spice. The PDO covers Asenovgrad, Parvomai and Sadovo municipalities. Legend ties the grape's name to a young man of Khan Krum's time whose wine-fuelled courage saved the vineyards.
bg-asenovgrad.nerd_note: Mavrud vines are often trained low and need a long, warm autumn; the best old vines sit on the alluvial terraces of the Chaya river below the Rhodope foothills.

bg-bolyarovo.name: Bolyarovo
bg-bolyarovo.summary: Bolyarovo, near the Turkish border south-east of Yambol, was registered in 2009 as the last of Bulgaria's PDOs. Its municipality is a remote, hot strip of vineyard on the eastern Sakar plateau.

bg-brestnik.name: Brestnik
bg-brestnik.summary: Brestnik, a village in the Rodopi municipality just south of Plovdiv, has its own PDO for reds from Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet and Merlot grown on the first Rhodope foothills. Its slopes rise just above the Maritsa plain, where the alluvial soils give way to the stonier ground that Mavrud prefers.

bg-chernomorski-rayon.name: Chernomorski Rayon
bg-chernomorski-rayon.grapes: Dimyat, Riesling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer, Muscat Ottonel
bg-chernomorski-rayon.summary: Chernomorski Rayon ('Black Sea Region') is the broadest Bulgarian PDO, covering 47 municipalities of north-east Bulgaria from Dobrich and Varna to Shumen, Razgrad and Silistra. It is the umbrella for the region's whites.

bg-dolinata-na-struma.name: Dolinata na Struma
bg-dolinata-na-struma.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Melnik 55, Keratsuda, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah
bg-dolinata-na-struma.summary: Dolinata na Struma ('Struma Valley') is the broad PDO covering 22 municipalities along the Struma from Pernik and Kyustendil south to Petrich and Sandanski, including Blagoevgrad and Kresna. It frames all the south-west's wine styles, from Broadleaf Melnik and Melnik 55 to Cabernet, Merlot and the rare Keratsuda white of Kresna.

bg-dragoevo.name: Dragoevo
bg-dragoevo.summary: Dragoevo, a village near Veliki Preslav, has a small white-wine PDO in the Novi Pazar and Veliki Preslav municipalities. Its vineyards lie on the same limestone plateau as Preslav's, below the 10th-century capital's ruins. Today the name is rarely seen on labels.

bg-evksinograd.name: Evksinograd
bg-evksinograd.summary: Evksinograd (Euxinograd) is the former royal summer palace on the coast just north of Varna, built in the 1880s for Prince Alexander of Battenberg. Its estate vineyards give their name to a tiny PDO.

bg-han-krum.name: Han Krum
bg-han-krum.summary: Han Krum, a village named after the 9th-century khan of the Mavrud legend, has a large winery long known for white wines, especially Chardonnay and Traminer. Its PDO covers three municipalities around Shumen and Preslav.

bg-harsovo.name: Harsovo
bg-harsovo.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Melnik 55, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
bg-harsovo.summary: Harsovo, a village in the Sandanski municipality near Melnik, gives its name to a small PDO in the heart of Broadleaf Melnik country. Villa Melnik's estate is nearby. Like the rest of the Struma valley it enjoys the warm air that funnels north from the Aegean.

bg-haskovo.name: Haskovo
bg-haskovo.grapes: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Mavrud, Rubin
bg-haskovo.summary: The Haskovo PDO spans six municipalities in the south-east, from the Rhodope foothills to the Sakar hills. Castra Rubra, named after a nearby Roman fort, is the region's flagship estate.

bg-hisarya.name: Hisarya
bg-hisarya.summary: Hisarya is a Roman spa town with intact 4th-century walls. Its municipality includes Starosel, where the Thracian temple complex of Chetinyova Mogila stands near a modern winery and spa built around the wine-and-Thracians theme.

bg-ivaylovgrad.name: Ivaylovgrad
bg-ivaylovgrad.summary: Ivaylovgrad is in the far south-east near the Greek border, in the warm eastern Rhodopes, close to the Roman villa of Armira with its mosaics. Its PDO is for reds, especially Mavrud and Merlot.

bg-karlovo.name: Karlovo
bg-karlovo.grapes: Misket Cherven, Muscat Ottonel, Riesling, Cabernet Sauvignon
bg-karlovo.summary: Karlovo, at the western end of the Rose Valley beneath the Balkan range, covers five municipalities. The area is known for Misket and Red Misket whites. Karlovo is also where the Rose Valley's oil-rose harvest begins each May, and the valley's sheltered position between two mountain ranges keeps its whites aromatic and fresh.

bg-karnobat.name: Karnobat
bg-karnobat.grapes: Misket Cherven, Muscat Ottonel, Rkatsiteli, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
bg-karnobat.summary: Karnobat, inland from Burgas, covers the Karnobat and Straldzha municipalities. It makes whites and reds, and is historically a big brandy and wine centre. Its position between the Black Sea and the eastern Balkan range gives a mild climate suited to both aromatic whites and Bordeaux reds.

bg-lom.name: Lom
bg-lom.summary: Lom, a Danube port in the north-west, has a single-municipality PDO for reds and whites from loess terraces above the river. Lom was one of Bulgaria's main Danube ports, and its river terraces are warm and well drained.

bg-lovech.name: Lovech
bg-lovech.summary: Lovech, at the foot of the central Balkan range, has a small single-municipality PDO for reds and whites from cooler, hillier ground. The town sits on the Osam river where the plain meets the Balkan foothills, so its vineyards are a little cooler and later-ripening than those of the Danube lowlands.

bg-lozitsa.name: Lozitsa
bg-lozitsa.summary: Lozitsa, whose name means 'little vine', is a village in the Nikopol municipality on the Danube. It has a small PDO for wines from the loess bluffs. Nikopol was an important Danube fortress town, and the north-facing river terraces give fresh, medium-bodied wines.

bg-lyaskovets.name: Lyaskovets
bg-lyaskovets.summary: Lyaskovets, near Veliko Tarnovo, has a long winemaking tradition and a winery known for sparkling and still wines; the PDO covers its municipality. Lyaskovets is a few kilometres from Veliko Tarnovo, capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire, and its winery has a long tradition of traditional-method sparkling wine.

bg-lyubimets.name: Lyubimets
bg-lyubimets.summary: Lyubimets covers the eastern Sakar hills and the lower Maritsa (Harmanli, Lyubimets, Stambolovo, Svilengrad and Topolovgrad municipalities). It is warm Merlot and Cabernet country, and the former state cellar at Lyubimets was a major exporter.

bg-melnik.name: Melnik
bg-melnik.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55), Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
bg-melnik.summary: The Melnik PDO covers the Petrich municipality around the tiny town of Melnik, Bulgaria's smallest with about 400 inhabitants, set among the sandstone and conglomerate 'earth pyramids' that rise up to 100 m above the Struma valley. Its grape is Shiroka Melnishka Loza (Broadleaf Melnik), a late-ripening red with small, dark berries that ripens in October and makes spicy, tobacco-scented, oak-loving wines; Melnik 55, its early-ripening offspring bred at Sandanski in 1963, is softer and riper. Melnik wine has been recorded since at least 1346, was shipped to Venice and beyond from merchants' rock-cut cellars such as the Kordopulov House (1754), and is said to have been Winston Churchill's favourite Bulgarian wine.
bg-melnik.terroir: Sandy and sandstone soils at the foot of the Pirin; hot, dry sub-Mediterranean climate funnelled up the Struma valley.
bg-melnik.nerd_note: Shiroka Melnishka Loza is a parent of Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55), whose other parent DNA testing identified as the French Valdiguié.

bg-montana.name: Montana
bg-montana.summary: Montana covers nine municipalities in the north-west between the Balkan range and the Danube; Gamza and Cabernet are the main reds. The area's limestone and loess soils and continental climate give medium-bodied reds, and Gamza here is light and peppery.

bg-nova-zagora.name: Nova Zagora
bg-nova-zagora.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Mavrud, Chardonnay
bg-nova-zagora.summary: Nova Zagora covers six municipalities east of Stara Zagora, including Chirpan and Sliven's southern edge, and is the only Bulgarian PDO registered for quality sparkling wine as well as still wine. Edoardo Miroglio's estate at Elenovo and Midalidare near Chirpan are the leading producers.

bg-novi-pazar.name: Novi Pazar
bg-novi-pazar.summary: Novi Pazar, east of Shumen on the north-eastern plateau, has a small PDO for whites (registered with the Veliki Preslav municipality). It shares the limestone-rich plateau and cool, breezy conditions that made the Shumen-Preslav area Bulgaria's white-wine heartland under socialism.

bg-novo-selo.name: Novo Selo
bg-novo-selo.summary: Novo Selo, a Danube village in the Vidin province, is the classic home of Gamza (Kadarka), which makes light, peppery, red-fruited wines here; the PDO covers its municipality. The Danube moderates temperatures, letting the late-ripening, thin-skinned grape reach full ripeness without losing its freshness.

bg-oryahovitsa.name: Oryahovitsa
bg-oryahovitsa.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Rubin, Mavrud, Syrah
bg-oryahovitsa.summary: Oryahovitsa, a village near Stara Zagora on the southern slopes of the Sredna Gora, is home to the Oriachovitza winery, founded in 1936, which became famous in the 1980s for Cabernet-Merlot blends exported to the UK. Its own vineyards sit at 170 to 260 m.

bg-pavlikeni.name: Pavlikeni
bg-pavlikeni.summary: Pavlikeni, in the central north, has a single-municipality PDO. Its winery was another of the export-era Cabernet and Merlot producers. Its loess-covered hills between the Danube and the Balkan range give medium-bodied, fruity reds, and Gamza also grows here.

bg-pazardzhik.name: Pazardzhik
bg-pazardzhik.grapes: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Mavrud
bg-pazardzhik.summary: The Pazardzhik PDO lies in the upper Maritsa valley west of Plovdiv (registered with the Septemvri municipality). The area's best-known modern estate is Bessa Valley, founded in 2001 by Count Stephan von Neipperg of Château Canon-la-Gaffelière and Karl-Heinz Hauptmann, which makes Merlot-led reds.

bg-perushtitsa.name: Perushtitsa
bg-perushtitsa.summary: Perushtitsa, south-west of Plovdiv at the foot of the Rhodopes, is the second classic home of Mavrud; its PDO covers part of the Rodopi municipality. The town is also a national shrine for its role in the April Uprising of 1876.

bg-pleven.name: Pleven
bg-pleven.summary: Pleven is home to Bulgaria's Institute of Viticulture and Enology, where Rubin was bred in 1944, and a wine museum in a cave in Kaylaka park. Its PDO covers four municipalities.

bg-plovdiv.name: Plovdiv
bg-plovdiv.grapes: Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pamid
bg-plovdiv.summary: Plovdiv, the ancient Philippopolis, is the centre of the Thracian Lowlands; its PDO takes in eight municipalities around the city (Asenovgrad, Kuklen, Perushtitsa, Rodopi, Saedinenie, Brezovo, Parvomai). Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot dominate, and the Brestovitsa area is known for Rubin.

bg-pomorie.name: Pomorie
bg-pomorie.grapes: Dimyat, Muscat Ottonel, Riesling, Cabernet Sauvignon
bg-pomorie.summary: Pomorie, on a peninsula on the southern Black Sea coast near Burgas, covers four municipalities and is known for Dimyat whites and for grape brandy. The sea moderates temperatures and lengthens the season.

bg-ruse.name: Ruse
bg-ruse.grapes: Riesling, Chardonnay, Traminer, Muscat Ottonel, Cabernet Sauvignon
bg-ruse.summary: Ruse, on the Danube opposite Giurgiu in Romania, covers six municipalities. It is known for whites (Riesling, Chardonnay, Traminer) and some reds; the city was the 19th-century gateway for Western wine culture.

bg-sakar.name: Sakar
bg-sakar.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Mavrud, Cabernet Franc
bg-sakar.summary: Sakar is a low mountain on the Turkish border near Svilengrad, a historic vineyard area that has become one of Bulgaria's most dynamic since 2000. Its warm, dry slopes on granite and sandy soils grow Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah and Mavrud. Katarzyna and Terra Tangra are the best-known estates.

bg-sandanski.name: Sandanski
bg-sandanski.grapes: Melnik 55, Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Sandanski Misket, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
bg-sandanski.summary: Sandanski, at the foot of the Pirin in the Struma valley, is one of Bulgaria's warmest wine towns. Its research station bred Melnik 55 in 1963, and the local Sandanski Misket is a rare aromatic white. The PDO covers the Sandanski municipality.

bg-septemvri.name: Septemvri
bg-septemvri.summary: Septemvri, at the western end of the Thracian plain where the Maritsa leaves the mountains, has a PDO for its municipality, mainly for reds from Cabernet, Merlot and Pamid. It sits close to the cooler air descending from the Rila and Rhodope mountains, so the wines are fresher than those of the eastern plain.

bg-shivachevo.name: Shivachevo
bg-shivachevo.summary: Shivachevo, a small town in the Tvarditsa municipality at the foot of the Balkan range, has a small PDO for reds and whites from sheltered slopes. The Balkan range protects the vineyards from northern winds, and the area's old cooperative supplied reds for the export trade.

bg-shumen.name: Shumen
bg-shumen.grapes: Chardonnay, Traminer, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel, Aligoté
bg-shumen.summary: Shumen, on the plateau of north-east Bulgaria near the medieval capitals Pliska and Preslav, covers Shumen, Novi Pazar and Veliki Preslav municipalities. It is known for whites, especially Chardonnay, Traminer and Riesling, from the large Shumen winery.

bg-slavyantsi.name: Slavyantsi
bg-slavyantsi.summary: Slavyantsi, a village in the Sungurlare valley, has its own small PDO, also centred on Red Misket and aromatic whites. Its vineyards share the valley's sheltered, cool-night conditions, which preserve the perfume of Misket. Few producers use the name today; most label their wine Sungurlare or Thracian Lowlands PGI.

bg-sliven.name: Sliven
bg-sliven.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pamid, Misket, Rkatsiteli
bg-sliven.summary: Sliven, below the Blue Rocks of the eastern Balkan range, covers four municipalities. Its large winery, Vini Sliven, was a key exporter, and the area grows both reds and whites.

bg-stambolovo.name: Stambolovo
bg-stambolovo.summary: Stambolovo, a village in the eastern Rhodope foothills near Haskovo, has a PDO for its municipality; its old cellar was known in the export era for Merlot. The hot, dry eastern Rhodope foothills ripen Merlot fully, and Stambolovo Merlot was a familiar export label in the 1980s.

bg-stara-zagora.name: Stara Zagora
bg-stara-zagora.summary: The Stara Zagora PDO covers the warm southern slopes of the Sredna Gora around the city of Stara Zagora (Bratya Daskalovi and Opan municipalities). It is red-wine country: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Rubin and Syrah.

bg-suhindol.name: Suhindol
bg-suhindol.summary: Suhindol, in the hills of the central Danubian plain, is a historic wine village whose cooperative, founded in 1909, is often called Bulgaria's first. In the 1980s its Cabernet Sauvignon and Gamza were among the bestselling Bulgarian wines in Britain. The PDO covers Suhindol and Pavlikeni.
bg-suhindol.nerd_note: Suhindol's cooperative was founded as 'Gamza' in 1909, named after the local grape, decades before the state took over the industry.

bg-sungurlare.name: Sungurlare
bg-sungurlare.grapes: Misket Cherven, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel, Traminer
bg-sungurlare.summary: Sungurlare's valley, in the eastern Balkan foothills, is the classic home of Misket Cherven (Red Misket), a pink-skinned aromatic white that gives delicate, floral, slightly spicy wines. The PDO covers Sungurlare, Karnobat and Kotel municipalities.

bg-svishtov.name: Svishtov
bg-svishtov.summary: Svishtov, on the Danube at Bulgaria's northernmost point, covers the Svishtov and Belene municipalities. Its winery was one of the main suppliers of Cabernet Sauvignon for the export boom, from vineyards on loess bluffs above the river.

bg-targovishte.name: Targovishte
bg-targovishte.grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel
bg-targovishte.summary: Targovishte, in the eastern Danubian plateau, covers the Targovishte and Loznitsa municipalities; its winery is known for Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Riesling. The plateau's cool nights and limestone-rich soils favour crisp whites, as across the north-east.

bg-varbitsa.name: Varbitsa
bg-varbitsa.summary: Varbitsa, in the Shumen province at the northern foot of the eastern Balkan range, has a small single-municipality PDO for whites and reds. The village sits in a sheltered valley where the eastern Balkan range meets the north-eastern plateau, so it combines Black Sea freshness with continental warmth.

bg-varna.name: Varna
bg-varna.summary: Varna's PDO covers the vineyards around Bulgaria's main port (Varna, Aksakovo and Byala municipalities). Coastal whites dominate, from Dimyat, Riesling and Chardonnay. The sea keeps autumns long and mild, so whites ripen slowly and keep their acidity.

bg-veliki-preslav.name: Veliki Preslav
bg-veliki-preslav.summary: Veliki Preslav was the capital of the First Bulgarian Empire in the 10th century. Its PDO covers three municipalities, and its old cellar was famous for Chardonnay and Traminer whites.

bg-vidin.name: Vidin
bg-vidin.grapes: Gamza, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay
bg-vidin.summary: Vidin, in Bulgaria's north-west corner, covers Vidin, Novo Selo and Belogradchik municipalities. It is Gamza country, and its estates include Bononia (named after Roman Vidin) and Magura, whose traditional-method sparkling wine ages in a cave decorated with prehistoric paintings near Rabisha.

bg-vratsa.name: Vratsa
bg-vratsa.grapes: Gamza, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay
bg-vratsa.summary: Vratsa covers seven municipalities of the north-west, from the Balkan foothills to the Danube at Oryahovo and Kozloduy. Burgozone (Oryahovo) and Tipchenitza (Mezdra) are leading estates. The stretch along the Danube is hot and dry, while the Iskar gorge near Mezdra is cooler, so the PDO covers quite different conditions.

bg-yambol.name: Yambol
bg-yambol.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pamid, Rkatsiteli, Muscat Ottonel
bg-yambol.summary: The Yambol PDO covers the Tundzha valley around Yambol and Elhovo (five municipalities). It is a large, warm, flat area of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and whites, once a major exporter.

bg-yuzhno-chernomorie.name: Yuzhno Chernomorie
bg-yuzhno-chernomorie.grapes: Dimyat, Riesling, Muscat Ottonel, Sauvignon Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
bg-yuzhno-chernomorie.summary: Yuzhno Chernomorie ('Southern Black Sea Coast') is a broad PDO covering 13 municipalities around Burgas, from Nesebar and Pomorie to Sozopol and Tsarevo. It is used for whites and reds from coastal and inland vineyards.

sites.name: Kordopulov House, Melnik
sites.text: Built in 1754 for wine production and later owned by the Greek merchant Manolis Kordopoulos, this house in Melnik has a tunnel cellar cut into the sandstone with ventilation shafts and channels. It can hold about 300 tonnes of wine, and its largest cask holds 12.5 tonnes. It is now a museum and tasting room.

sites.name: Melnik Earth Pyramids
sites.text: Rain has carved Neogene sandstone capped with reddish conglomerate into towers, mushrooms and obelisks up to 100 m high around Melnik. They are a natural landmark since 1960, covering about 17 km². The town's wine cellars are dug into the same soft rock.

sites.name: Melnik
sites.text: Bulgaria's smallest town, with about 400 people, Melnik once had some 20,000 and traded wine to Venice, Austria and England. It lies among the earth pyramids at the foot of the Pirin, and Broadleaf Melnik is grown in the surrounding valleys.

sites.name: Rozhen Monastery
sites.text: About 6 km north-east of Melnik, Rozhen is the largest monastery in the Pirin region, with roots in the medieval period. Vines grow on the slopes below it, and a trellis of old vines shades its courtyard.

sites.name: Thracian temple of Chetinyova Mogila, Starosel
sites.text: This Thracian temple under a mound near Starosel dates from the late 5th to early 4th century BC. It is the largest of six underground temples in the Starosel complex, found in 2000. A local winery has built its identity around the Thracian cult of wine.

sites.name: Starosel wine complex
sites.text: A winery, hotel and spa outside Starosel, built in Thracian-revival style with cellars dug into the hillside. It makes reds and whites under the Hisarya PDO near the village's Thracian temples.

sites.name: Perperikon
sites.text: A rock-cut sacred city on a 470 m hill near Kardzhali in the Eastern Rhodopes, occupied from about 5000 BC to the 14th century. A famous temple of Dionysus is thought to have stood here, and its rock altar is almost 2 m across.

sites.name: Magura Cave and winery
sites.text: Magura Cave near Rabisha in the north-west has prehistoric paintings in bat guano. Since the 1980s it has also housed the cellar of a traditional-method sparkling wine, aged in the cave's constant 12 °C.

sites.name: Pleven Wine Museum, Kaylaka
sites.text: Pleven's wine museum occupies a natural cave in Kaylaka park, displaying several thousand bottles and the history of Bulgarian winemaking. Pleven's institute bred Rubin in 1944.

sites.name: Suhindol
sites.text: This hill village in the central north founded Bulgaria's first wine cooperative, 'Gamza', in 1909. In the 1980s its Cabernet Sauvignon was a bestseller on British supermarket shelves.

sites.name: Asenovgrad
sites.text: Asenovgrad, at the mouth of the Chaya gorge below the Rhodopes, is the traditional capital of Mavrud. The legend of Khan Krum and the brave youth Mavrud is set here. The medieval Asen fortress and Bachkovo Monastery are nearby.

sites.name: Sungurlare valley
sites.text: The Sungurlare valley in the eastern Balkan foothills is the home of Red Misket (Misket Cherven). This pink-skinned aromatic white gives delicate, floral wines, and the town holds a wine festival each autumn.

sites.name: Euxinograd Palace
sites.text: Euxinograd, the former royal summer palace on the coast north of Varna, was built in the 1880s for Prince Alexander of Battenberg. Its park and estate vineyards give their name to a small PDO.

sites.name: Brestovitsa
sites.text: A village south-west of Plovdiv on the Rhodope foothills, known for Rubin and Mavrud. Georgiev & Milkov make Rubin here, and the area once supplied the Plovdiv export cellars.
